## VIC rejection and rollback: four guards, a latch and redo cause 32 (`forward_masked`) {#sec-ch07-vic-reject}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** When any column of a block cannot be solved, or any value around the solve is not finite,
undoes the correction for the whole block, skips the solve in the remaining stages, and asks for the step to be
redone.
**Switch.** None; always on with the VIC.
**Order.** Not a discretisation.
**Defining equation.** None; see the list of guards in the Derivation.
:::

The VIC never applies a partial or nonfinite correction. A failure is turned into a clean "no correction" for
the stage. It is latched for the rest of the step and becomes cause 32 of the step acceptance
in @sec-ch07-redo, which restores the step input and halves the step.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the section states the guards and the invariants they keep. `forward_masked` checks,
in this order:

1. the latch: a failure earlier in the step returns a zero correction without solving;
2. the inputs: `du`, `w` and $\gamma$ finite in every interior column;
3. the sentinel: no NaN left in the solution by a refused column (@sec-ch07-vic-sweep);
4. the results: the corrected `du` and the redistribution buffer finite;
5. the correction: `du` after minus `du` before finite.

A refusal at guards 2 to 5 restores `du` and `w` from copies taken on entry and returns a zero correction. Both
copies are bit for bit the inputs [check `src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_reject_check.py`, output
`vic_reject_check.out`, `[C1]`]. It also sets the latch and logs the rank, column, step, stage and retry. After a
failure at stage 0 the other two stages of rk3 do not solve (`[C2]`). The latch raises redo cause 32. The reset
at stage 0 of the retry lets the retry solve again (`[C3]`). One failed column out of four gives a zero
correction for every column of the block, so no column is partly updated (`[C4]`).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-reject for the guards.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-reject
#| fig-cap: "The path through forward_masked. The latch (white) returns a zero correction for the rest of a failed step. The four guards (orange) each lead to the same refusal (vermillion): restore du and w, return a zero correction, set the latch and log the column, which check_redo reads as cause 32. A pass through all of them returns du - du0 (green)."
#| fig-alt: "A row of seven boxes, latch, input check, solve, sentinel check, redistribution, result check and correction check, with arrows from the four checks down to a single refusal box."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_reject import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The latch is `_solve_failed` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:175-180`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L175-L180)). Its accessors are
`reset_solve_failure` and `solve_failed` ([`implicit_hydro.hpp:96-101`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp#L96-L101)). On entry the module copies
`du` into `_du0` and clones `w` into `w0` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:195-198`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L195-L198)). The refusal is the
lambda `reject` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:200-218`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L200-L218)). The guards are `bad_inputs`
([`implicit_hydro.cpp:222-224`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L222-L224)), `bad_columns` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:348-351`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L348-L351)),
`bad_results` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:473-475`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L473-L475)) and `bad_correction`
([`implicit_hydro.cpp:480-481`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L480-L481)). The guards are block-wide reductions. On a GPU each costs a device
to host transfer of one flag.

The step-acceptance flags read the latch as `solve_failure` ([`meshblock.cpp:858-862`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L858-L862)). Stage 0 of
every step attempt calls `reset_solve_failure` ([`meshblock.cpp:616-619`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L616-L619)). A VIC failure is the one
cause that still restores the step after `max_redo` (@sec-ch07-redo).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A failure discards the work of the whole block for the step, and of every block, since the redo decision is
global. A column that fails at every step size stops the run after `max_redo` retries.
:::

1. **Block-wide.** One bad column zeroes the correction of all columns of its block (`[C4]`). This is the price
   of having no per-column status channel.
2. **Synchronising guards.** Each guard reads a flag back to the host.
3. **Not cured by a smaller step.** A float32 column refused for its conditioning may be refused again at every
   halving (@sec-ch07-vic-pivot).
